results.answer: The Magellanic Woodpecker (Campephilus magellanicus), known in Chile as Carpintero negro, is a large woodpecker of the temperate and subantarctic forests of Chile and Argentina whose cavities are later used by more than 20 bird species. It lives in mature Nothofagus and Araucaria forests with senescent trees — such a remarkable bird! It shows strong sexual dimorphism, with mostly black plumage and white on the wings, the male with crimson-red head and crest and the female with a mostly black head and red near the base of the bill.
